formality: Formal 'Anda' address throughout the UI (never 'kamu', never regional slang) — the standard register for Indonesian professional/enterprise software, while still reading like a tool built by and for practitioners rather than a government form.
styleNotes: Keep hashcat/pentest jargon that the Indonesian infosec/CTF community already uses as English loanwords (hash, wordlist, rule, mask, keyspace, chunk, job, agent, crack) rather than forcing a formal dictionary translation — this community code-switches heavily for CS/security terms, more so than for generic business vocabulary. Translate everyday UI/business words naturally into Indonesian (pengaturan, prioritas, anggaran, notifikasi) instead of defaulting to English. For mixed noun phrases, use Indonesian noun-adjective word order (e.g. 'file rule', 'keyspace efektif', 'potfile klien') instead of literal English order. Where a loanword needs an Indonesian affix, use the productive 'ter-'/'di-' tech-slang pattern (tercrack, di-crack) already used for terupdate/terinstall/terupload, rather than inventing a formal verb (avoid 'memecahkan', 'menguras', 'pembongkaran' for crack/drain/teardown).

hash.note: Universal in Indonesian security tooling and hashcat documentation; translating it (e.g. to 'nilai hash') would be unrecognizable to practitioners.

hashlist.note: KrakenHashes-specific product concept (an uploaded set of hashes); kept as the product's own noun, consistent with hash/wordlist/potfile staying English.

crack.note: Fixed from draft's 'memecahkan': loanword verb standard in Indonesian pentest/CTF writing, used even in formal academic security papers ('teknik cracking password', 'proses crack hash'); 'memecahkan' reads like breaking a physical object and 'membobol' implies unauthorized break-in, the wrong connotation for a cryptographic recovery step. Keep consistent with sibling hashcat terms (wordlist, rule, mask, keyspace) that stay English.

cracked.note: Fixed from draft's 'terpecahkan': uses the productive Indonesian tech-slang pattern of 'ter-' + English loanword root (parallel to 'terupdate', 'terinstall', 'terupload'), matching 'crack' staying English. Natural for the short status labels/badges ('Status: Tercrack', 'Belum Tercrack') this term is used for throughout the analytics UI.

cracked hashes.note: Fixed from draft's 'hash yang terpecahkan': combines 'hash' (kept English) with 'tercrack' (see cracked), mirroring how 'hash reuse' keeps 'hash' untranslated while Indonesian-izing the modifier.

plaintext.note: Industry-standard term; 'teks biasa'/'teks polos' would be technically correct but unrecognizable next to 'hash'/'potfile' on the same screen.

potfile.note: hashcat's own filename/concept; not translated in any language's security tooling.

wordlist.note: Industry standard; 'daftar kata' is too generic and reads like a vocabulary list, not an attack resource.

rule.note: hashcat-specific mangling rule; 'aturan' is correct Indonesian for 'rule' in general but loses the specific hashcat-rule-syntax meaning.

mask.note: hashcat-specific attack-pattern term (e.g. ?u?l?l?d); no natural Indonesian equivalent in this context.

charset.note: Standard technical computing term; kept in English as in other Indonesian technical documentation.

brute force.note: Fixed from draft's bare 'brute force': matches the parallel structure of the sibling attack-type values ('serangan kamus', 'serangan hibrida', 'serangan asosiasi') so all four attack-mode options read consistently in a dropdown; 'brute force' itself stays untranslated since there is no single-word Indonesian equivalent.

keyspace.note: Standard cryptographic/hashcat term; 'ruang kunci' is a literal gloss nobody uses in practice.

effective keyspace.note: 'keyspace' kept as in the base term; 'efektif' is the translation.

chunk.note: KrakenHashes-specific work-distribution unit; kept English as in Indonesian devops usage ('dibagi jadi beberapa chunk').

task.note: Standard term in distributed-systems/devops Indonesian usage.

job.note: Industry standard (as in Kubernetes Jobs, Jenkins, cron); 'pekerjaan' reads as generic employment/work and loses the scheduling-system meaning.

preset job.note: KrakenHashes-specific concept kept fully English, matching the project's own English UI convention (CLAUDE.md: 'Preset Job Management', not a translated title).

workflow.note: Standard term in Indonesian technical/business software; matches the 'Workflow' domain entity name used internally.

loopback.note: KrakenHashes-specific feature name as well as a standard networking term; kept English like other named features (workflow, preset job).

max agents.note: Fixed from draft's 'agen maksimal': 'agent' is kept English everywhere else in this glossary and in the project's own UI convention (CLAUDE.md: 'Agent Management', not 'Agen Management'); translating only the plural noun in this one setting label while keeping 'agent' English elsewhere was inconsistent.

overflow.note: Technical scheduling term (extra agents beyond a job's limit); kept English like 'chunk'/'task', standard in Indonesian computing usage (cf. 'buffer overflow').

benchmark.note: Standard in Indonesian technical documentation; also a hashcat CLI term.

hash rate.note: Standard measurement term in the hashcat/mining community.

progress.note: Fixed from draft's 'kemajuan': 'progres' is the standard absorbed Indonesian software term for a completion percentage/progress bar; 'kemajuan' reads as general real-world advancement (e.g. 'kemajuan ekonomi'), not a UI progress indicator.

agent.note: Standard term in distributed computing; also the project's own English UI entity name.

device.note: Standard in technical UI for a GPU/CPU; 'perangkat' is correct but less standard in this specific hardware-device sense.

voucher.note: Standard loanword in Indonesian e-commerce and technical systems (voucher diskon, voucher pulsa) and matches the product's own 'voucher' noun.

heartbeat.note: Standard term for periodic check-in signals in Indonesian network/systems monitoring; a literal translation would read like a human heartbeat.

offline buffer.note: Fixed from draft's literal 'buffer offline': this is a grace period before an agent is marked offline, not a data buffer. 'Masa tenggang' is the standard Indonesian term for a grace period ('masa tenggang pembayaran', 'masa tenggang SIM card') and matches the actual concept.

binary.note: Common as-is in Indonesian developer/release jargon ('unduh binary hashcat'); no natural Indonesian noun is used for this in practice.

client.note: Professional term for a customer/engagement in Indonesian IT/consulting.

password reuse.note: Fixed from draft's 'penggunaan ulang sandi': use the full 'kata sandi' rather than bare 'sandi', which alone can also mean 'code/cipher' (e.g. 'sandi morse') and is ambiguous out of context.

hash reuse.note: 'hash' kept English as elsewhere; matches the fixed phrasing of 'password reuse'.

domain.note: Standard in Active Directory/Windows security context; paired with 'username' in the same cracked-hash tables (username@domain).

username.note: Fixed from draft's 'nama pengguna': displayed alongside 'domain' in the same AD/cracked-hash context (username@domain, table columns); keeping 'domain' English while translating 'username' would make adjacent, paired column headers inconsistent.

SAN.note: Acronym for Subject Alternative Name; the full Indonesian translation is too long for certificate UI and nobody expands the acronym in practice.

network share.note: Fixed from draft's 'berbagi jaringan': that phrase is the verb/gerund 'sharing a network' (e.g. a mobile hotspot), not the noun for a mounted SMB/NFS resource — wrong concept, not just a style choice. SMB/NFS are already kept English (doNotTranslate) and Indonesian sysadmins overwhelmingly use English-only tooling (no official Indonesian AWS/Azure/GCP/Samba localization) for this exact term, so 'network share' stays English rather than inventing an unused Indonesian noun.

mount.note: Standard term in filesystem/storage contexts, including Indonesian Linux documentation.

cloud fleet.note: 'armada' (fleet) is a natural, understood metaphor already used in Indonesian ride-hailing/logistics tech ('armada kendaraan'); 'cloud' stays as the loanword since 'awan' reads as a textbook/BSSN term that working engineers don't actually use for cloud infrastructure.

drain.note: Fixed from draft's 'menguras': this is the Kubernetes/orchestration sense (stop scheduling new work, let in-flight work finish), not physically draining/emptying something. No official Indonesian localization of this devops concept exists (kubectl, cloud consoles are English-only for Indonesian users), and 'menguras' only carries the literal/physical meaning and loses the scheduling sense entirely.

teardown.note: Fixed from draft's 'pembongkaran': an IaC/cloud-ops term for deprovisioning an instance, paired with 'provisioning' and 'drain' in the same cloud-fleet lifecycle. 'Pembongkaran' reads as physical demolition/disassembly; no official Indonesian cloud-console localization exists to anchor a natural translated alternative, so it stays English like 'drain'.

webhook.note: Standard term in web development and API contexts.

branding.note: Standard marketing/UI loanword in Indonesian business usage; matches the project's own 'branding' feature naming.
